content.user_title: Run and Configure Oxlint for JavaScript and TypeScript
content.value_statement: Lint diagnostics and inconsistent configurations can slow JavaScript and TypeScript maintenance. This skill guides project-aware Oxlint checks, focused fixes, rule configuration, and ESLint migration.
actual_capabilities: Identify existing Oxlint usage through dependencies, configuration files, and package scripts before recommending lint commands.
Guide whole-project or targeted file checks, interpret diagnostics, and apply standard automatic fixes.
Explain rule severities, categories, plugins, environment globals, and file-specific configuration overrides.
Guide shared configuration inheritance, nested monorepo configurations, and type-aware lint settings.
Select diagnostic output formats and warning thresholds for CI workflows.
Explain side-by-side ESLint integration and configuration conversion with the Oxlint migration utility.
limitations: The skill contains instructions only; it does not bundle Oxlint, its dependencies, or an execution environment.
Commands and plugin support depend on the installed Oxlint version and project configuration.
ESLint migration requires reviewing unsupported rules and plugins; complete rule parity is not established by this guide.
For Vue, Svelte, and Astro files, the guide limits lint coverage to script blocks.

use_cases.title: Check Frontend Changes
use_cases.description: Lint edited React or TypeScript files, explain diagnostics, and resolve issues without unnecessary rule suppressions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Monorepo Rules
use_cases.description: Review shared configurations, package overrides, plugin selection, and type-aware settings across multiple project directories.

use_cases.title: Prepare CI Lint Checks
use_cases.description: Choose diagnostic formats and warning thresholds while planning a staged transition from ESLint.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Check Project Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether this project uses Oxlint. Identify its dependency, configuration, and lint script. Recommend the existing lint command without changing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: First review of an unfamiliar JavaScript or TypeScript project.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Resolve Diagnostics
prompt_templates.prompt: Lint the files I changed using this project's Oxlint setup. Explain diagnostics, apply standard safe fixes, and report remaining issues. Avoid unsafe transformations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused lint cleanup after a code change.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Review Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this monorepo's Oxlint configuration. Propose shared defaults, package overrides, and relevant plugins. Preserve existing coverage and explain any type-aware requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Plan ESLint Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this project's ESLint setup with Oxlint coverage. Propose a staged migration, flag unsupported rules, and define CI checks. Request approval before installing migration dependencies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Controlled migration with explicit dependency review.

output_examples.input: Check how linting should run in a project with Oxlint installed and a lint script.
output: Project detection: Oxlint is declared and the lint script invokes it.
Recommended action: Use the existing project lint script.
Fix policy: Use standard automatic fixes; unsafe transformations require an explicit request.

output_examples.input: Recommend a baseline configuration for an existing TypeScript project.
output: Baseline: Treat correctness issues as errors and suspicious patterns as warnings.
Plugins: Preserve the intended plugin list when editing configuration.
Type-aware checks: Confirm TypeScript configuration before enabling them.
Validation: Run lint checks and review configuration changes.

output_examples.input: Explain a cautious path from ESLint to Oxlint.
output: Start with side-by-side checks and remove duplicate rule reporting through the integration plugin.
Review migration utility output before replacing the existing ESLint configuration.
Keep unsupported ESLint checks until equivalent coverage is established.

best_practices: Confirm existing Oxlint usage and inspect the project lint script before running commands.
Review automatic fix changes, rerun relevant checks, and reserve suppressions for genuine false positives.
Verify installed-version support and review dependency changes before migration or plugin installation.
anti_patterns: Running Oxlint in a project without evidence that it is used.
Applying unsafe transformations without an explicit user request.
Replacing ESLint or suppressing diagnostics before checking rule coverage and understanding the underlying issues.

faq.question: Does this skill install Oxlint automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides existing Oxlint projects and includes optional migration commands. Review dependency installations before running them.

faq.question: Can I use this skill with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The report lists all three tools as supported. Running commands requires an environment with project files and shell access.

faq.question: Can it lint only changed files?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions show how to pass specific project file paths to Oxlint.

faq.question: Are all automatic fixes safe?
faq.answer: No. The guide recommends standard fix mode and requires an explicit request for dangerous transformations. Review diffs and run project tests.

faq.question: Will Oxlint fully replace my ESLint rules?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. The skill describes coexistence and migration, but rule and plugin compatibility must be reviewed for your project.

faq.question: Can it configure monorepos and type-aware linting?
faq.answer: It documents nested configurations, shared configuration inheritance, and type-aware options. Confirm installed-version support and the required TypeScript configuration.
